ety.text: The verb is from Middle English amen, aimen, eimen (“to guess at, to estimate, to aim”), borrowed from Old French esmer, aesmer, asmer, from Latin ad- plus aestimare (“to estimate”), the compound perhaps being originally formed in Medieval Latin (adaestimare), perhaps in Old French. The noun is from Middle English ame, from Old French aesme, esme.

senses.d: The pointing of a weapon, as a gun, a dart, or an arrow, or object, in the line of direction with the object intended to be struck; the line of fire; the direction of anything, such as a spear, a blow, a discourse, a remark, towards a particular point or object, with a view to strike or affect it.
ex: Take time with the aim of your gun.

senses.d: The level of accuracy of a weapon.
ex: A rifle has more precise aim than a shotgun.

senses.d: The point intended to be hit, or object intended to be attained or affected.

ex: My number one aim in life is to make money to make my parents, siblings, and kids happy.

senses.d: The ability of someone to aim straight; one’s faculty for being able to hit a physical target.
ex: The police officer has excellent aim, always hitting the bullseye in shooting practice.
He has a bad aim, so he decided to join archery classes.
What you would work me to, I have some aim.

senses.d: To point or direct a missile, or a weapon which propels as missile, towards an object or spot with the intent of hitting it
ex: He aimed at the target, but the arrow flew straight over it.

senses.d: To direct the intention or purpose; to attempt the accomplishment of a purpose; to try to gain; to endeavor;—followed by at, or by an infinitive
ex: to aim to do well in life

senses.d: To direct or point (e.g. a weapon), at a particular object; to direct, as a missile, an act, or a proceeding, at, to, or against an object
ex: to aim an arrow at the deer
She aimed a punch at her ex-boyfriend.

senses.d: To direct (something verbal) towards a certain person, thing, or group
ex: to aim a satirical comment at Communists in general
But, good my lord, do it so cunningly / That my discovery be not aimed at;
